questions.prompt: Which best describes cryptocurrency?
choices: Digital money that runs on a decentralized network
A coin minted by the U.S. Treasury
A type of government savings bond
A physical gold coin you hold in your hand
questions.explanation: Crypto is digital-only money that lives on a computer network no single company or government controls.

questions.prompt: Cryptocurrency is issued and guaranteed by a national government.
questions.explanation: Unlike dollars or euros, most crypto has no government behind it promising its value.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that crypto is 'decentralized'?
choices: No single company or government is in control
One big bank runs the whole thing
The United Nations approves every payment
It only works when you are offline
questions.explanation: Decentralized means power is spread across many computers instead of one central boss.

questions.prompt: Which are true of most cryptocurrencies? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: They are digital-only
They run on a decentralized network
Their prices can swing sharply
They are insured by the FDIC
questions.explanation: Crypto is digital, decentralized, and volatile, but it is NOT FDIC-insured like a bank deposit.

questions.prompt: Sort each item into cryptocurrency or government money.
questions.explanation: Crypto lives on blockchains with no central issuer; government money is printed and backed by a nation.

questions.prompt: Crypto prices can be very volatile, sometimes moving 10% or more in a single day.
questions.explanation: Big, fast price swings are normal in crypto, which makes it risky for money you might need soon.

questions.prompt: Why is it called 'crypto'?
choices: It uses cryptography to secure transactions
It must be kept in a crypt
It is completely invisible
It is always illegal
questions.explanation: The name comes from cryptography, the math that keeps transactions secure and hard to fake.

questions.prompt: What is a blockchain?
choices: A shared digital ledger that records transactions
A single Excel file on one laptop
A physical stack of coins
A private government database
questions.explanation: A blockchain is a shared record of transactions, copied across many computers at once.

questions.prompt: Once data is confirmed on a blockchain, it is extremely hard to change.
questions.explanation: Blocks are locked together with cryptography, so altering old records is nearly impossible.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a blockchain transaction in order.
items: The transaction is broadcast to the network
It is bundled into a new block
The block is linked onto the chain
questions.explanation: Send, broadcast, verify, bundle into a block, then link the block to the chain.

questions.prompt: What do miners or validators do?
choices: Verify transactions and add new blocks
Print new dollar bills
Delete old transactions for fun
Set the country's interest rates
questions.explanation: Miners and validators do the work of checking transactions and adding them to the chain.

questions.prompt: Why is a blockchain hard to tamper with? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: Copies are stored across many computers
Blocks are cryptographically linked together
One person can quietly edit it alone
Changing one block breaks the whole chain
questions.explanation: Many copies plus linked blocks mean no single person can secretly rewrite history.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: A computer that helps run the network
No single central authority in charge
questions.explanation: These are the core building blocks: a ledger of blocks, kept by nodes, with no central boss.

questions.prompt: A blockchain is stored on a single central computer owned by a bank.
questions.explanation: The opposite is true: it is copied across many independent computers, which is what makes it decentralized.

questions.prompt: Bitcoin is often nicknamed...
choices: Digital gold
A digital cash printer
The internet dollar
A stablecoin
questions.explanation: Bitcoin has a limited supply and is seen mainly as a store of value, like gold.

questions.prompt: Ethereum is best described as...
choices: A platform for apps and smart contracts
A currency printed by a government
A physical hardware wallet
A savings bank
questions.explanation: Ethereum is a programmable platform where developers build apps, not just a simple coin.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: A platform for apps and smart contracts
Where you store your crypto keys
The secret code that controls your crypto
questions.explanation: Coins and platforms differ, and your wallet holds the keys that prove ownership.

questions.prompt: Your private key is like a password that lets you spend your crypto, so you must keep it secret.
questions.explanation: Anyone who has your private key can move your crypto, so never share it.

questions.prompt: Which are true about crypto wallets and keys? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: Your public address can be shared to receive funds
Your private key must stay secret
A wallet stores your keys
Sharing your private key with others is perfectly safe
questions.explanation: Share your public address freely, but guard your private key like a password.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a coin and a token?
choices: A coin has its own blockchain; a token is built on another blockchain
A coin is physical; a token is digital
They are exactly the same thing
A token is always worth more than a coin
questions.explanation: Coins like Bitcoin run their own chain, while tokens ride on top of a chain like Ethereum.

questions.prompt: If you lose your private key, there is usually a 'forgot password' button to recover your crypto.
questions.explanation: There is no reset button in crypto, so losing your key usually means losing your coins forever.

questions.prompt: What is the golden rule of crypto investing?
choices: Only invest what you can afford to lose
Always borrow money to buy more
Put all of your savings into one coin
Never do any research first
questions.explanation: Because crypto is so volatile, only risk money you could lose without wrecking your life.

questions.prompt: Crypto held on an exchange or in a wallet is insured by the FDIC like a bank deposit.
questions.explanation: There is no FDIC protection for crypto, so if it is lost or stolen, no one guarantees it back.

questions.prompt: You invest $500 in a coin and it drops 80%. How many dollars is your holding worth now?
questions.explanation: An 80% drop leaves 20%, and 20% of $500 is $100.

questions.prompt: What is a 'rug pull'?
choices: Creators hype a project, take investors' money, then vanish
A way to earn guaranteed interest
A type of extra-secure wallet
A government tax on crypto gains
questions.explanation: In a rug pull, the founders disappear with the money, leaving investors with worthless coins.

questions.prompt: Which are smart crypto safety habits? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: Only invest what you can afford to lose
Back up your keys somewhere safe
Share your private key with helpful strangers
Be skeptical of promises of guaranteed returns
questions.explanation: Protect your keys and your money, and never hand your private key to anyone.

questions.prompt: Match each risk to its description.
pairs: No way to recover access to your coins
Founders take the money and disappear
Losses are not insured by the government
questions.explanation: Knowing the main risks helps you spot trouble before it costs you.

questions.prompt: A project promising guaranteed high returns with no risk is a classic warning sign of a scam.
questions.explanation: No real investment guarantees big returns with zero risk, so that promise is a red flag.

questions.prompt: What is a stablecoin?
choices: A crypto designed to hold a steady value, often pegged to $1
A coin that always doubles in price
A physical silver coin
A government savings bond
questions.explanation: Stablecoins aim to stay near a fixed value like $1, so they swing far less than Bitcoin.

questions.prompt: What is an NFT?
choices: A unique digital token that proves ownership of a specific item
A stablecoin pegged to gold
A type of credit card
A bank account for crypto
questions.explanation: NFT means non-fungible token, a one-of-a-kind digital certificate of ownership.

questions.prompt: What does DeFi (decentralized finance) mean?
choices: Financial services like lending and trading built on blockchains without traditional banks
A government finance department
A savings account at a normal bank
A crypto exchange owned by a bank
questions.explanation: DeFi recreates banking-style services using code on a blockchain instead of a bank.

questions.prompt: Sort each description into stablecoin, NFT, or DeFi.
items: Lending or trading crypto without a bank
Often pegged to the US dollar
Proves you own a unique piece of digital art
questions.explanation: Stablecoins hold value, NFTs prove ownership, and DeFi offers bank-like services on-chain.

questions.prompt: A stranger DMs you promising to double any crypto you send them. This is a scam.
questions.explanation: 'Send me crypto and I'll send back double' is one of the oldest scams around.

questions.prompt: Which are common crypto scam red flags? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: Promises of guaranteed profit
Pressure to act fast right now
Requests for your private key or seed phrase
Using a well-known regulated exchange
questions.explanation: Guarantees, urgency, and key requests scream scam; a reputable exchange is not itself a red flag.

questions.prompt: NFTs and DeFi carry no risk because they use blockchain technology.
questions.explanation: Blockchain does not remove risk; NFTs and DeFi can still lose value or be exploited by hackers.

questions.prompt: Which best describes cryptocurrency?
choices: Digital money on a decentralized network, not issued by a government
Paper money printed by the Federal Reserve
A savings account at a credit union
A government-backed bond
questions.explanation: Crypto is digital, decentralized, and not backed by any government.

questions.prompt: Cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin are backed and guaranteed by a national government.
questions.explanation: No government stands behind Bitcoin's value, which is part of what makes it different and risky.

questions.prompt: A blockchain is best described as...
choices: A shared, tamper-resistant ledger of transactions
A single private file owned by one bank
A physical vault full of gold
A secret government spreadsheet
questions.explanation: A blockchain is a shared ledger copied across many computers, making it hard to fake.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a blockchain transaction.
items: It is broadcast to the network
It is added to a new block
The block is linked to the chain
questions.explanation: Create, broadcast, confirm, add to a block, then link it to the chain.

questions.prompt: Why is Bitcoin nicknamed 'digital gold'?
choices: It has a limited supply and is seen as a store of value
The government guarantees its price
It is physically made of gold
It can never lose value
questions.explanation: Like gold, Bitcoin's supply is capped and many treat it as a long-term store of value.

questions.prompt: You put $1,000 into a coin and it falls 25%. What is your holding worth now?
questions.explanation: A 25% drop leaves 75%, and 75% of $1,000 is $750.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: Secret code that controls your crypto
Crypto pegged to a steady value like $1
Unique token proving ownership of an item
questions.explanation: These are key ideas from across the unit: keys, stablecoins, NFTs, and validators.

questions.prompt: Which are warning signs of a crypto scam? (Choose all that apply.)
choices: Promises of guaranteed returns
A request for your private key or seed phrase
Pressure to act immediately
Trading on a regulated, well-known exchange
questions.explanation: Guarantees, key requests, and urgency are classic scam signals; a reputable exchange is not.

questions.prompt: Sort each statement into Bitcoin or Ethereum.
items: A platform for smart contracts and apps
Designed mainly as a store of value
Powers many tokens and DeFi apps
questions.explanation: Bitcoin is mainly a store of value; Ethereum is a programmable platform for apps.

questions.prompt: Money you keep on a crypto exchange is FDIC-insured just like a bank account.
questions.explanation: Crypto is not FDIC-insured, so only risk what you can afford to lose and guard your keys.
